units.title: Extremal argument for a set closed under an LCM quotient
units.statement: Let S contain positive integers and suppose for every a<b in S, the difference b−a divides lcm(a,b) and the quotient belongs to S. Write a=gu,b=gv with gcd(u,v)=1. Divisibility forces v−u=1, so b−a=g divides a. With m=min S, all members are m+d for divisors d of m, hence S is finite. Write M=max S=d(u+1),m=du. Since u(u+1)=lcm(m,M)/(M−m) lies between m and M, d is u or u+1. Any intermediate b=m+s has s<d and s|m; putting v=m/s≥u+1 gives lcm(m,b)/(b−m)=v(v+1)>M, a contradiction. Thus |S|≤2. Its two-member forms are {u²,u(u+1)} and {u(u+1),(u+1)²}.
steps: Reduce each pair to coprime factors and show its difference equals its gcd
Use the minimum to establish finiteness and inspect the maximum
Rule out an intermediate member through an LCM quotient above the maximum
